This is a proposal in a funding application, not an approved or built project. The article gives no hydrogen-hub acreage.
facts.reference: Land of opportunity: Former Umatilla Chemical Depot could become regional hydrogen hub
facts.quote: Obsidian's map showed the depot as its Oregon hub, with another near Moses Lake, Washington.

facts.summary: EPA Region 10 recognized the Umatilla Army Depot Superfund site in 2024 with its Howard Orlean Excellence in Site Reuse Award. The EPA page says the authority designated 5,500 acres of the land as a wildlife refuge, and the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation obtained 4,000 of the acres, which the page describes as an important cultural site. The page gives only the year, so no date is recorded.
facts.reference: EPA Region 10 Howard Orlean Excellence in Site Reuse Award
facts.quote: The authority designated 5,500 acres of this land as a wildlife refuge.

facts.summary: On November 27, 2017 the Oregon Adjutant General and the US Army Corps of Engineers signed a license dedicating 7,500 of the depot's 19,729 excess acres as a new Oregon National Guard Training Center. The DVIDS article was posted January 11, 2018. This is a land-use designation, not a development project.
facts.reference: Big changes for Camp Umatilla
facts.quote: that dedicates 7,500 acres of the former depot's 19,729 acres as a new Oregon National Guard Training Center.

TND073540783.name: ILLINOIS CENTRAL RAILROAD COMPANY'S JOHNSTON YARD SUPERFUND SITE
gaps: Searched Johnston Yard, Harrison Yard, Horn Lake Road and redevelopment terms. No 2025-2026 coverage of a reuse, sale or new tenant for the yard was found.

Found but not cited: CN completed a $100 million Memphis yard reconstruction (American Journal of Transportation, Sept. 2009) and renamed it Harrison Yard. The page I opened does not name Johnston Yard, and its address (297 Rivergate Road) differs from the Superfund address (2921 Horn Lake Road), so I could not confirm the match.
An EPA reuse page (search snippet only, not opened) says an intermodal cargo transfer facility operated on the site until 2006. Not cited: it is historical use, not a development project.
Current operating status of the yard was not verified.

facts.summary: Progressive Railroading (April 20, 2006) reported that Canadian National would spend $100 million to rebuild and upgrade Johnston Yard in Memphis, with completion planned for late 2008. This is an upgrade of an operating rail yard, not a redevelopment for other uses. The article gives no street address, so the link to this Superfund site rests on the matching yard name and city.
facts.reference: CN to rebuild century-old Memphis yard
facts.quote: it will spend $100 million to rebuild and upgrade Johnston Yard in Memphis, Tenn.

TXD980810386.name: SOUTH CAVALCADE STREET
gaps: Searched Cavalcade and Maury Street with redevelopment, toll road and 2025-2026 terms. No 2025-2026 news of a reuse or development project for this site was found.
ABC13 report on residents' groundwater worries and EPA institutional-control statements (abc13.com/archive/9000197) has no date on the page, so it is not cited.
ABC13 article of March 28, 2024 on the Hardy Toll Road downtown extension approval does not mention Cavalcade, the Superfund site or a construction start. Not cited.
The Houston Chronicle quote came from a model-processed page extract, not the raw page text. Check the exact wording against the live page before relying on it.
The Maury Street search returned only a commercial listing for 2206 Maury St, with no link to the site.

facts.summary: Houston Chronicle (Nov. 30, 2013) reported that the Harris County Toll Road Authority planned a $350 million extension of the Hardy Toll Road into downtown through part of the 66-acre site south of Cavalcade, with construction expected to begin in 2020. This was a 2013 proposal. I found no 2024-2026 coverage tying the extension to this site. A March 2024 ABC13 article on the approved extension does not mention Cavalcade or the Superfund site.
facts.reference: Superfund cleanup to move at nature's pace
facts.quote: is planning a $350 million extension of the Hardy Toll Road into downtown through part of the site.

TXD980873343.name: NORTH CAVALCADE STREET
gaps: Searched North Cavalcade with news, development and 2025 terms. No development project, developer, incentive or redevelopment news was found.
Houston Chronicle (Nov. 30, 2013) mentions a wood-treatment plant north of Cavalcade added to the cleanup list, but the article does not name North Cavalcade. Not cited.
The undated ABC13 institutional-controls report (see South Cavalcade) is not cited.
The EPA 2018 five-year review (an agency document, not news) says the remedy is protective. Not cited here.

UTD070926811.name: KENNECOTT (NORTH ZONE)
gaps: Searched Kennecott North Zone, Magna, 2100 South and 12000 West with data center, West Bench and redevelopment terms. No 2025-2026 local news about a project at or near this site was found.
12000 West and 2100 South falls outside Magna's core street grid according to one source. The exact parcel is not confirmed as a redevelopment site.
A September 2026 Salt Lake Tribune data center story is about Juab County (Nebo North LLC, near Mona), not Magna. Not cited.
A 2023 Salt Lake Tribune story on Rio Tinto's Bingham Canyon tailings expansion is not tied to the North Zone in the text I read. Not cited.
Kennecott Land's West Bench residential plans (from a 2008 KSL search snippet, not opened) are not cited.
Utah DEQ's proposed-sites page lists the North Zone as a proposed NPL site. It is an undated agency page, not news, so it is not cited as a fact.

facts.summary: KSL (Aug. 26, 2008) reported that the North Zone, like the South Zone, was placed on the proposed Superfund list in 1994, and that Kennecott officials hoped the North Zone would be taken off the proposed list in the coming years. The article is mainly about the South Zone's expected removal. The sources I found show the North Zone still on the proposed list.
facts.reference: Kennecott site to stay off Superfund list
facts.quote: Kennecott officials are hoping the North Zone will be taken off the proposed list in the coming years.

facts.summary: A U.S. EPA Region 8 hearing clerk filing dated Oct. 1, 2025 lists an Administrative Settlement Agreement and Order on Consent for the Kennecott North Zone Site, docket CERCLA-08-2026-0001 (the docket year is 2026, the filing date 2025). The attached PDF names operable units OU22 and OU23. The page does not state the order's purpose or terms, so this is a dated cleanup-enforcement record, not a redevelopment commitment.
facts.authority: U.S. EPA Region 8 Regional Hearing Clerk
facts.reference: Administrative Settlement Agreement and Order on Consent, CERCLA-08-2026-0001
facts.quote: Kennecott North Zone Site (CERCLA-08-2026-0001).

ACRES-121721.name: Former Salvage Yard
gaps: Searched the site name, the street address (3745 South 3rd Street, Ironton) and Ironton redevelopment terms. No news, council, or agency item names this address or a salvage yard at it.

The Ohio Round 11 brownfield list (May 2026) and the Ironton coverage of it name a Lawrence County Port Authority project 'Ironton Iron' ($90,000 cleanup). The Tribune and WSAZ say it is a former iron foundry and give no street address, so it is not matched to this site and is left out.
The same May 2026 coverage names a '3rd Street BiLo #44' former gas station in Ironton, with no address. Not matched and left out.
The EPA-cited Wilson Glove Building (1603 S. 3rd St.) on the 3rd Street corridor is a different property and is left out.
Directory listings (for example, Ohio Valley Crash Parts at 3217 S 3rd St) are aggregators and were not used as evidence.

CA2570024453.name: GEORGE AIR FORCE BASE
gaps: Searched George AFB with data center, 2026 and redevelopment terms. No data center proposal, developer, or news was found for this site.
The Air Force data center solicitations found in search (Edwards AFB, Tucson, Alaska sites) are other bases and are left out.
An Air Force Civil Engineer Center article on the logistics redevelopment at George AFB returned HTTP 403 to both the fetch and the web reader, so it is not cited.
San Bernardino County and City of Victorville council records were not searched; the tools available here do not reach those systems.

facts.summary: EPA's redevelopment profile says the proposed reuse was an international airport and railway hub, plus commercial, industrial and business park development. EPA says this is on hold because of economic conditions. The page is undated.
facts.reference: EPA Superfund redevelopment profile, GEORGE AIR FORCE BASE (id 0902737)
facts.quote: this is on hold due to economic conditions

facts.summary: EPA's profile says current reuse is commercial and industrial: 17 aviation-related businesses, an aircraft mechanics training program, manufacturing and distribution centers, a multi-million dollar power plant, and a 900-acre federal prison complex. These are existing uses, not new projects. The page is undated.
facts.reference: EPA Superfund redevelopment profile, GEORGE AIR FORCE BASE (id 0902737)
facts.quote: 17 aviation-related businesses

FLSFN0407002.name: JACKSONVILLE ASH SITE
gaps: Searched the site name, the 1093 West 6th Street address and Lonnie Miller Park terms. The news pieces name the park, not the street address. The address is tied to the Lonnie Miller area by the EPA profile, which lists 1093 West 6th Street for this site.
An August 2026 story on a shooting near a game at the park is about safety, not redevelopment, and is left out.
No news found on whether the sports complex named in the EPA profile is funded or approved. The city's Capital Projects page and the EPA remedial project manager were not reached.
The EPA profile is undated, so the redevelopment-plan fact carries no date.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says future redevelopment is planned for the Lonnie Miller Park area, including a proposed sports complex with soccer fields, baseball diamonds and basketball courts. The profile gives no timeline, funding or approval status, and no date.
facts.reference: EPA Superfund site profile, JACKSONVILLE ASH SITE (id 0407002)
facts.quote: sports complex with soccer fields, baseball diamonds, and basketball courts

facts.summary: The city plans to clean up Lonnie C. Miller Park, which was once used to dump incinerator ash. The city then gave summer 2025 as the goal for finishing the ash cleanup. This is a News4JAX story republished by Jacksonville Today.
facts.reference: Jacksonville plans cleanup at park once used as dump site
facts.quote: The city says the goal is to get the contaminated ash site cleaned up by the summer of 2025

facts.summary: Residents said the city was slow to start removing the hazardous material. The city said the cleanup would take about a year. Phase two, the park remodel, was projected to cost over $12 million.
facts.reference: Residents express frustration over delayed ash cleanup at Jacksonville's Lonnie Miller Park
facts.quote: Phase two, which includes park remodeling, is projected to cost over $12 million

facts.summary: The City of Jacksonville is running the cleanup and upgrade of the park. The city split the project into two phases so part of the park can reopen sooner.
facts.reference: City invests more than $22M for cleanup, upgrades at Lonnie C. Miller Regional Park in NW Jacksonville
facts.quote: The city divided the project into two phases to allow part of the park to reopen sooner

facts.summary: The city puts more than $22 million into removing the old incinerator ash and upgrading the park. Plans include athletic fields, trails, pavilion space and parking. The city expects completion by the end of 2026, later than the summer 2025 goal given in December 2024.
facts.reference: City invests more than $22M for cleanup, upgrades at Lonnie C. Miller Regional Park in NW Jacksonville
facts.quote: remediation costs totaling more than $22 million

FUDS-A04MS0124.name: GULFPORT ARMY AIR FIELD
gaps: Searched the field name and Gulfport former airfield redevelopment for 2025 and 2026. No redevelopment plan, developer, incentive or news was found for the former field.
The 2019 USACE FUDS information guide (A04MS0124) describes the former field and its skeet range, including lead shot. It names no reuse plan and is not news, so it is not cited as a fact.
Gulfport Harbor lease (October 2026) and the downtown Channel South project (March 2026) are other properties and are left out.

The Gulfport-Biloxi International Airport is a joint-use airport with an Air National Guard base. It is an existing use, not a redevelopment, and no source here ties it to a reuse decision for the former field.

FUDS-B07MO0173.name: TYSON VALLEY POWDER FARM
gaps: Searched the site name, Eureka, and Lone Elk Park with 2025 and 2026 terms. No news, county, or developer item on a current project, sale, or cleanup at the Powder Farm was found.
The Powder Farm is also called Lone Elk Park and West Tyson County Park. The park items found are undated (a radio segment and a bison-calf item with no year), so none are cited.
The 2018 EPA award is the most recent dated item found, and it names no county. St. Louis County parks releases and Army Corps FUDS records were not checked.

facts.summary: EPA Region 7's 2018 release says the Tyson Valley Powder Farm won a national Federal Facility Excellence in Site Reuse award in the non-NPL category. It describes reuse already in place: the Washington University Tyson Research Center's Endangered Wolf Center, Lone Elk Park and a World Bird Sanctuary. This recognizes existing reuse, not a new project.
facts.reference: Tyson Valley Powder Farm in Eureka, Mo., Wins National Federal Facility Excellence in Site Reuse Award
facts.quote: Now, the site hosts the Washington University Tyson Research Center's Endangered Wolf Center

FUDS-E05IL0102.name: SANGAMON ORDNANCE PLANT
gaps: Searched the site name, Illiopolis, the water tower, and Formosa Plastics cleanup for 2024 to 2026. No redevelopment, developer, incentive, or cleanup news for the ordnance plant land was found. The 2024 to 2025 Formosa hits concern a St. James Parish, Louisiana project and are excluded.

A 2024 News-Gazette column (Tom Kacich) reports that most of the land has returned to farming and that the Illiopolis water tower was designated a county landmark. Opening it returned HTTP 429, so nothing from it is cited. Verify before use.
An Illinois Times item on a proposed landmark for the water tower is undated in the results and was not opened, so it is not cited.
The only agency cleanup record opened is the May 2005 fact sheet. Groundwater, soil, and dioxin remedy status after 2005 is not verified.

facts.summary: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4 (May 2005) on the Formosa Plastics site west of Illiopolis, the former Borden PVC plant within the ordnance plant land. The state did not yet know the extent of the chemicals left on site, and it said the remedial investigation would not fully start until demolition was complete. The sheet is about 20 years old, and no later agency status was found.
facts.reference: Formosa Plastics site, Illiopolis: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4
facts.quote: The Illinois EPA does not yet know the extent of chemicals that remain.

FUDS-I04FL0038.name: RICHMOND NAS
gaps: Searched the site name, Richmond Heights, Chapman Field, and Zoo Miami or Metrozoo planning for 2024 and 2025. No current development project, developer, incentive, or cleanup news for the former air station land was found.
Most 'Richmond' results were other places (Richmond VA Navy Hill, Richmond Heights MO, Richmond Heights OH) and are excluded.

A search result mentions an April 2024 approval for a historical marker at the Miami-Dade Military Museum, in the former station headquarters building. It was not opened and is a museum item, so it is not cited.
Whether the 2000 master plan was completed is not verified.

facts.summary: Miami Today reported in July 2000 that Portico Group was selected to create a new master plan for Metrozoo and the former Richmond Naval Air Station in South Dade. The plan was to be covered by $12 million in 1996 Safe Neighborhood Park bond funds, with a final document expected in April 2001. The article covers planning only, not reuse of the base, and no outcome was found.
facts.reference: Firm Named To Redesign Plan For Zoo Richmond Base
facts.quote: to create a new master plan for Metrozoo and the former Richmond Naval Air Station in South Dade.

FUDS-I04NC0485.name: CHARLOTTE ARMY MIS PL
gaps: Matched to this site because the Mecklenburg County landmark record identifies the Charlotte Quartermaster Depot / Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road as 'the Camp Road property now comprising Camp North End'. News coverage uses the Hercules Industrial Park and Camp North End names.
The Axios February 2026 article on Jamestown returned HTTP 403 and was not opened. Nothing from it is cited.
No dated, opened source was found for the phase-two plans beyond the 2026 entitlement figure. The WSOC next-phase headline was not opened in full.
Kinship's completion date is not verified from an opened page.
Acreage differs by source (72 acres in the rezoning story, 75 to 76 acres for the site). Not resolved.
No community benefit, incentive, or cleanup item was found in news for this site.

facts.summary: WFAE reported in July 2017 that ATCO bought the roughly 75-acre site in December 2016 for about $17 million. The new owners planned to keep the historic plant buildings and make the site resemble its 1920s look. The rezoning from general industrial to mixed-use was still pending then.
facts.reference: Former Model T missile factory: redevelopment part of Camp North End
facts.quote: ATCO, which bought the 75-acre site last December for about $17 million.

facts.summary: Charlotte City Council approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development in September 2017. The county landmark record names this site the Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road. At the time, ATCO's plans called for up to 1,500 apartments and 1.5 million square feet of office space.
facts.reference: Council approves 72-acre Camp North End rezoning
facts.quote: The Charlotte City Council on Monday approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development

facts.summary: WSOC reported in May 2023 that work was underway on Atco Properties' first apartment community at Camp North End, Kinship. It is a two-building, 240,390-square-foot project with 301 units and an estimated completion in early 2025. The article quotes plans to eventually develop up to 1,800 total units on the site. Completion was not verified.
facts.reference: Work first apartments coming to Camp North End begins
facts.quote: Work is underway on Atco Properties’ first apartment community at Camp North End.

facts.summary: Atlanta-based Jamestown joined the ownership of the 76-acre Camp North End as general partner and lead asset manager. ATCO remains a partner, and Shorenstein remains a partner in a portion of the project. The investment amount was not disclosed. PointBlank Ventures was retained to raise joint-venture equity for the next phases.
facts.reference: Jamestown Joins Ownership Group at 76-Acre Camp North End Campus in Charlotte
facts.quote: Jamestown has partnered with existing ownership to recapitalize Camp North End

facts.summary: WFAE reported in February 2026 that the property is entitled for up to 3.2 million square feet of additional development. The new owners said they want more housing, retail, and food and beverage tenants. The article gives no phase plan or unit count.
facts.reference: Changes in ownership at Camp North End
facts.quote: The property is entitled for up to 3.2 million square feet of additional development.

FUDS-I04NC0594.name: WINSTON-SALEM ARPT
gaps: Searched the Winston-Salem airport and Smith Reynolds with redevelopment and former Army airfield terms. Found the 2025 FBO renovation and a 2025 terminal renovation, but no redevelopment of the former military land.
The match between the FUDS record and Smith Reynolds Airport rests on name and wartime history, not a boundary match. The record's acreage is null.
The Smith Reynolds site plan (SRA_Site_Plan_5.pdf) describes available land for lease. It was seen in search and not opened, so no lease or development fact is cited from it.

facts.summary: Signature Aviation reopened a renovated fixed-base operator (FBO) of about 3,000 sq ft in the airport terminal, which dates to 1941. The reconstruction took two years. The article reports a completed tenant renovation, not a redevelopment of former Army airfield land. The FUDS record name is Winston-Salem Airport, matched here to Smith Reynolds Airport by name and airport history.
facts.reference: Signature Debuts Updated North Carolina FBO
facts.quote: celebrating the grand reopening of its renovated FBO this week at Smith Reynolds Airport (KINT)

FUDS-I04SC0025.name: CONWAY BMB&GUNRY RNG
gaps: Searched the Conway range with solar, development and cleanup terms. Found no solar project or other development sited on the range itself. The Bucksport solar farm near Conway is not tied to the range by any source found.
The 2018 article refers to 'a former Horry County bombing range'. I did not confirm that it names the Conway Bombing and Gunnery Range by name, so the match rests on the county-wide range identity.
A Corps focus on a 455-acre site in Carolina Forest surfaced in search but its page was not opened, so no fact is cited from it.

facts.summary: WBTW reports that the Army Corps of Engineers plans to propose no additional remediation on nearly 56,000 acres of the former Conway Bombing and Gunnery Range. The proposal follows a 2018 Corps report that found no longer any explosive hazards or human-health or environmental risks on the property. The page shows no publication date ('3 years ago' only).
facts.reference: Army Corps of Engineers plans no more remediation at site of former Conway Bombing and Gunnery Range
facts.quote: plans to propose that no additional remediation take place on nearly 56,000 acres of land

facts.summary: My Horry News reports that Horry County requires range properties to be identified in public records, a policy updated in 2003. Anyone pulling a construction permit inside the former bombing range must acknowledge that the property sits within an impact safety zone. The article reports three flagged areas (296, 1,525 and 495 acres) totaling about 2,316 acres, which the federal report found hold explosives.
facts.reference: Report: former Horry County bombing range sites pose unacceptable risk
facts.quote: county officials require that range properties be identified in public records

FUDS-K06TX0015.name: CAMP HOWZE
gaps: Searched Camp Howze with solar, rail park and development terms. Found no solar project on the camp grounds. North Gainesville Solar is a separate plant on N. Weaver Street and is not tied to the camp by any source found.
The rail park is one 480 to 489-acre part of the 58,702-acre FUDS property. Facts here describe that part only.
The developer's release page was opened. The page does not give a construction start date beyond the June 2026 groundbreaking.
No incentive (tax abatement, TIF, grant) coverage was found in the pages opened. The incentive search was not completed.

facts.summary: KXII reports the groundbreaking of Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park on June 18, 2026. KXII gives 480 acres; the developer's release gives 489 acres. The developer's release says the park is planned for up to 7 million square feet across 14 buildings. The park is a part of the former camp, not the whole 58,702-acre FUDS property.
facts.reference: Groundbreaking held for Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park in Gainesville
facts.quote: 480-acre development just off Interstate 35 in northwest Gainesville.

facts.summary: Stream Realty Partners is leasing the Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park on behalf of B-29 Investments in partnership with Hughes Commercial, according to the release. The release calls the park a 489-acre master-planned industrial development in Gainesville.
facts.reference: Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park breaks ground in Gainesville, Texas
facts.quote: are leading leasing efforts for the project on behalf of B-29 Investments in partnership with Hughes Commercial

facts.summary: KXII reports one anchor tenant has signed, with potential for up to 2,000 jobs. The tenant is not named, and the article presents the jobs as potential, not a commitment. The first industrial partner is named as Buzzi's, which is targeting the same year but has not broken ground.
facts.reference: Groundbreaking held for Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park in Gainesville
facts.quote: One anchor tenant is already signed on, with potential for up to 2,000 jobs.

IA7213820445.name: IOWA ARMY AMMUNITION PLANT
gaps: Searched IAAAP redevelopment and the Commerce Center. Found the July 2026 Army groundbreaking and the 2016 Commerce Center certification. No news on Commerce Center tenants, occupancy or sales since 2016 was found.
A 2014 Tri-States piece on commercial development possibilities at the plant and a 2026 report of a temporary plant closure for a safety review were seen in search and not opened.
No community benefit, host payment or cleanup-to-residents commitment was found.

facts.summary: The U.S. Army marked a July 15 groundbreaking for the Future Artillery Complex at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, a multi-million-dollar expansion of the Army's artillery production base for end-to-end production of 155 mm melt-pour ammunition. The article is dated July 22, 2026 and is an Army release, which does not name a private developer.
facts.reference: Army breaks ground on state-of-the-art ammunition plant in Iowa
facts.quote: officially launched the construction of the Future Artillery Complex

facts.summary: Tri-States Public Radio reports that the state certified part of the plant as the 12th Iowa Certified Site and that the property is 'ready for development'. IEDA head Debi Durham made the statement. American Ordnance, the plant's operator, is named in the story. The certified site is the Commerce Center described in the next fact.
facts.reference: Iowa Army Ammo Plant deemed 'Ready for Development'
facts.quote: the property is ready for development

facts.summary: The Commerce Center of Southeast Iowa is a 152.9-acre certified industrial site on federal land inside the plant, near Middletown. An act of Congress raised the land lease from 25 to 50 years to allow the site. The site is also BNSF rail-served certified. Partners named in the 2016 certification are the Iowa Economic Development Authority, the Greater Burlington Partnership and American Ordnance.
facts.reference: Burlington-area site joins 11 sites in Iowa that are part of the Iowa Certified Site program
facts.quote: it took an act of Congress to increase the lease duration on the land from the normal 25 years to 50 years.
